newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' Ramos offers to train successor.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' Ramos offers to train successor.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos has had one-on-one meetings with seven people aspiring to lead his party to victory and replace him in next year's general elections, a Presidential Palace statement said on Saturday.

Ramos met the presidential hopefuls, including his sister Senator Leticia Ramos Shahani, over a five-hour period on Friday. The other contenders in his ruling Lakas party are House of Representatives Speaker Jose de Venecia, Defense chief Renato de Villa, Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo, Presidential Adviser for Economic Affairs Lito Osmena, Senator Heherson Alvarez and Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office chairman Manuel Morato.

"Separately, they were asked about their determination to run for president, their visions and platform of government, their own assessment of their contributions to the current social and economic reform programmes of the administration and other reasons why they think they should be supported by the president and the party," the statement said.
The Lakas leaders agreed to recommend the holding of a convention in late November or early December to elect the party's standard bearer in the presidential race.
However, some Lakas members have asked Ramos to name his choice of successor before the convention.

During Friday's meetings, Ramos urged the presidential contenders to "have a feel of the job of a President by being with him in (Malacanang) palace for a specific period and also join at least one Cabinet meeting outside Malacanang," the statement added.
"The President stressed the need for sustaining the unity, solidarity and team work of all party leaders and members as the indispensable formula for the administration's victory in 1998 and beyond."
Ramos, whose six-year term ends in June 1998, is barred from seeking re-election.

Earlier, the Commission on Elections (Comelec) and the Supreme Court both denied the petition of a citizens' group to hold a referendum to change the Constitution and give Ramos a chance to run for a second term.
